$comment: The specs `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` runs, and the number of test blocks they contain.
MEASURED, not assumed. Every spec here was run against a full local Supabase
stack (Auth + Storage + `pnpm seed:demo`) on 2026-08-12 and passed with zero
skips. The full default suite in that run was 27 passed / 1 failed / 7 skipped,
and this list was exactly those 27. It has grown since — `expectedTestCount` below
is the authority on what it expects today; the 27 is a dated measurement, not a
running total.
`expectedTestCount` is a FLOOR the workflow asserts against the Playwright JSON
report. Its job is to catch a spec being renamed or moved out of the glob, which
would otherwise shrink CI coverage silently — the exact failure mode this whole
job exists to end. Update it deliberately when adding or removing a spec.
`support-access` is the newest addition (#958). It was excluded for timing out
after 120s on the `popup` event; the cause was never the spec but a missing admin
environment — `signSupportToken` threw, the route 500d, and the dialog returned
without opening the popup it was waiting for. It is the only spec anywhere that
covers support impersonation, so it is worth the second dev server it costs.
`admin-shell` (added with the Wave 1 admin console redesign) is UNMEASURED
against this stack — the worktree that authored it had no local Supabase and
`.env.local` resolves to production, so running it there was out of the
question. Its three locators (rail link + aria-current, the ⌘K command
palette, the notification tray) were instead verified by reading the
components they target (NavRail.tsx, AdminCommandPalette.tsx,
NotificationTray.tsx, lib/server/search/communities.ts) and cross-checked
against this same admin app's own jsdom unit tests (command-palette.test.tsx
confirms the cmdk combobox/option roles this spec relies on). The real
measurement is this job's own run on the PR that adds it — a failure there
is the gate doing its job, not a broken addition to this list.
`responsive-overflow` is UNMEASURED against this stack, on the same terms as
`admin-shell` above: the container that authored it had no Docker, no Supabase CLI
and no local Postgres, so running it there was impossible. It is registered anyway
because an unregistered spec gates nothing, and the regression class it exists to
catch (a viewport-keyed breakpoint firing inside a container ~340px narrower than
the viewport) had already shipped three broken screens past every other gate — one
of which a human reviewer then found still live in document-library.tsx after the
first fix. Its 4 blocks are 3 route x 4 viewport overflow checks plus one asserting
the app shell is absent from /pm/site-preview. The real measurement is this job's
own run on the PR that adds it; a failure there is the gate doing its job.
2026-09-14: `responsive-overflow` grew from 4 blocks to 5 (the `payments`
route) and its viewport list from 4 widths to 6 (375 and 414 added below the
old 768 floor), so expectedTestCount went 36 -> 37. The two new widths were
measured offline first -- real compiled CSS, real shell geometry, headless
Chromium -- rather than added on the hope that they pass. The `payments`
block is still UNMEASURED against this stack on the terms above.
2026-09-14, second round: `responsive-overflow` grew from 5 blocks to 8, so
expectedTestCount went 37 -> 40. The three added (`meetings`, `announcements
composer`, `settings`) each measured bleeding earlier in the same branch and
each has a different cause -- an inline-flex pill plus a 15px day-cell content
box, an implicit grid track sized to a datetime-local's intrinsic width, and a
loading skeleton with a hard w-64 -- so one regressing says something the
others would not. All three were measured at all six widths against a
production build before being added, and all three avoid record ids on
purpose: `/esign/submissions/[id]` bled too and is deliberately excluded,
because a block that 404s when the seed shifts is worse than no block. Like
`payments`, they are UNMEASURED against THIS stack (dev server + CI seed) --
this job's own run on the PR that adds them is the real measurement.
2026-09-17, review follow-up: `overflow-detector.spec.ts` joins the list (15
blocks) and expectedTestCount goes 40 -> 55. It drives `helpers/overflow.ts`
against synthetic `setContent` fixtures -- no server, no database, no seed --
so it is the one spec here that tests a GATE RULE rather than the app. That
rule had been wrong four separate times against a real app that answered
consistently every time, which is the failure a fixture test catches and a
page visit does not; writing it surfaced a fifth (reaching for scrollWidth
again made every `truncate` in the app report +236) and CI then surfaced a
sixth (trailing letter-spacing is counted by scrollWidth but painted by
nothing, so `tracking-[0.16em]` reported +2 and +3 on the meetings weekday
header). Both now have a case, each paired with its opposite.
COUNT THIS THE WAY THE WORKFLOW DOES. `playwright --list` prints warmup +
chromium; the assertion in e2e.yml filters `projectName !== warmup`. So the
floor is the CHROMIUM total, one less than the `--list` line. A draft of this
entry took the `--list` number, called the long-standing 40 a stale floor with
slack, and set 54 -- which CI rejected with `counted=53 floor=54`. The 40 was
right all along. Measure with:
playwright test --config playwright.ci.config.ts --list | grep -c chromium
Deliberately absent:
- signup-trialing / signup-failure-paths / signup-trial-end — self-skip without
Stripe secrets and are owned by stripe-e2e.yml. A skip here would be a green
run that proved nothing.
- onboarding-first-run — contains no runnable test, only two `test.fixme`
describing a wizard that was never built.
- pdfjs-runtime — owned by playwright.prod.config.ts; needs a production build
with PDFJS_TEST_ENABLED=1, which a dev server never sets.
- community-tenant-host-precedence / wave-2-ga-staging — owned by
playwright.tenant.config.ts; they need the tenant host on :3002.
